title: Meta turns off the Instagram feature that let users make AI deepfakes of public accounts
slides: Meta just killed your Instagram tool for AI clones.
Why remove a feature millions already used?
The real reason: legal battles no one saw coming.
Now you must ask permission for any public face.
Stop recycling old content—start creating original work.
thread_text:
1. Meta just killed your clone.

Over a million users built AI versions of themselves. The tool is now gone without warning.

2. Why remove what worked?

The feature drove daily engagement. But legal teams flagged a risk bigger than any metric.

3. Lawsuits nobody predicted.

Public faces used without explicit consent. GTA-like training data fights now hit social platforms.

4. Now you must ask permission.

Any face in a public dataset requires a signed release. The era of scraping ends here.

5. Test your own original content today.

Take one old post, rewrite it without recycling. Does the clone actually save time—or create more work?

instagram.caption:
Over a million users built AI versions of themselves on Instagram—and now the tool is gone without warning.

Meta killed the feature because legal teams flagged a massive risk: any public face used for training needs explicit permission. Lawsuits over scraping public data for AI clones finally caught up. 💥

Now, if you want to use someone's face in an AI tool, you need a signed release. The era of grabbing any public photo is over.

Do you rely on AI clones to save time—or do they just create new legal headaches for you? 🧠📸
